title: Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY scales to 60K notifications/s
summary: DBOS demonstrated that PostgreSQL&\#x27;s LISTEN/NOTIFY mechanism can handle 60,000 notifications per second, refuting earlier claims that it does not scale. This benchmark corrects a common misconception about PostgreSQL&\#x27;s notification system, showing it is viable for high-throughput real-time applications without requiring external message brokers. The test achieved 60,000 notifications per second using a single PostgreSQL instance, likely with optimized configurations, and the results were published with detailed methodology.
context: LISTEN/NOTIFY is a built-in PostgreSQL feature that allows client sessions to subscribe to channels and receive asynchronous notifications. A previous widely-circulated blog post claimed that LISTEN/NOTIFY does not scale for high-throughput use cases, leading many to avoid it. This new benchmark directly challenges that claim with measurable evidence.
discussion: Commenters noted that &\#x27;scale&\#x27; is a continuum and 60K/s may be insufficient for some but ample for many. Others referenced the earlier opposing article and appreciated the correction, while praising DBOS for leveraging PostgreSQL properly.
